predecessors.name: Majapahit
predecessors.text: Demak (Bintara) on the north coast of Central Java, a vassal of Majapahit 1475-1478

successors.name: Pajang Sultanate
successors.text: Pajang under Hadiwijaya (Jaka Tingkir), to whom the Demak regalia passed in 1568

ledger.x: 1475: Raden Patah's Demak appears as a vassal of Majapahit.
1518: Cliopatria's 1519 shape is six times the 1475 core; the page says Demak 'dominated Semarang, Jepara, Tuban, and Gresik' and that Trenggana 'took the remnants of Majapahit' (no year).
By 1518: Jambi under Demak's control; same undated page line as Palembang.
c. 1527: Demak conquers Tuban. 'Tuban, an old Majapahit port, was conquered' (the page's 'c. 1527').
1546: Trenggana killed at Pasuruan; Demak's reach over Sumatra is not recorded after this.
1546: as for Palembang; the page is silent.
1568: Arya Penangsang is killed and the sultanate ends.

wars.name: Demak war on Daha
wars.outcome: Patih Udara's Daha defeated in 1518; Raden Patah died soon after.

wars.name: Demak expeditions against Portuguese Malacca
wars.outcome: Both failed. The Demak page puts Pati Unus's first fleet (about 100 ships) in 1513 and the second (375 ships) in 1521, when he died; the Portuguese Malacca page has Demak sending ships in 1511 and a second campaign in 1521 'which also failed and cost the…

wars.name: Cirebon-Demak conquest of Sunda Kalapa and Banten
wars.outcome: Sunda Kalapa renamed Jayakarta; Banten under Hasanuddin as a province of Cirebon; peace with King Surawisesa in 1531.

wars.name: Trenggana's Pasuruan campaign
wars.outcome: Ended with Trenggana's death in 1546; no land changed hands.

certainty.note: A coastal sultanate whose reach is a list of ports and principalities; no treaty line is dated by the pages opened.
